paragraphs.title: The Armies Assemble and Goliath Issues His Challenge

easy.explanation: Israel pitched by the valley of Elah, opposite the Philistines.
easy.q: Where did Saul and the men of Israel pitch their camp?

easy.explanation: The champion was Goliath of Gath.
easy.q: Who came out of the Philistine camp as a champion?

answers: They were dismayed and greatly afraid
easy.explanation: The KJV says they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.
easy.q: How did Saul and Israel react when they heard Goliath’s words?

answers: Choose one man to fight him
medium.explanation: Goliath told Israel to choose a man and let him come down to fight.
medium.q: What did Goliath challenge Israel to do?

answers: Israel would become servants to the Philistines
medium.explanation: Goliath said the Israelites would be servants if he prevailed.
medium.q: What would happen if Goliath defeated Israel’s chosen man?

answers: A representative fighter chosen to face an opponent
A guard assigned to the king
medium.explanation: Goliath was the representative warrior of the Philistine army.
medium.q: What does the word “champion” mean in this passage?

answers: He threatened to burn their camp
He demanded that Israel leave the land
He was a huge, heavily armed warrior proposing a one-on-one battle
challenge.explanation: His great size, armor, weapons, and threats made him appear terrifying.
challenge.q: Why did Goliath’s challenge cause such fear among the Israelites?

answers: His apparent military strength and advantage
challenge.explanation: The description presents Goliath as heavily protected and powerfully armed.
challenge.q: What does the detailed description of Goliath’s armor emphasize?

answers: The valley between them provided a setting for representatives to meet
Both armies were inside the same city
Their positions had no relation to the challenge
challenge.explanation: The armies stood on opposite mountains with a valley between them, allowing a champion to come forward.
challenge.q: How were the armies’ positions related to Goliath’s proposal?

paragraphs.title: David and the Family of Jesse

easy.explanation: David was the son of Jesse the Ephrathite of Bethlehemjudah.
easy.q: Who was David’s father?

easy.explanation: The passage says that Jesse had eight sons.
easy.q: How many sons did Jesse have?

easy.explanation: David was the youngest.
easy.q: What was David’s position among Jesse’s sons?

medium.explanation: The three eldest sons were Eliab, Abinadab, and Shammah.
medium.q: Which three sons of Jesse followed Saul to battle?

answers: Between serving Saul and feeding his father’s sheep
medium.explanation: David went and returned from Saul to feed his father’s sheep.
medium.q: Between which responsibilities did David move?

medium.explanation: The Philistine presented himself morning and evening for forty days.
medium.q: How long did the Philistine present himself before Israel?

answers: He is the youngest and a shepherd, yet he becomes connected with the military conflict
He is already king but refuses to fight
He is the firstborn but unknown to his father
challenge.explanation: David is introduced as the youngest son caring for sheep while his older brothers are at war.
challenge.q: What central contrast is established in the presentation of David?

answers: Goliath’s threat was persistent and the fear continued over time
challenge.explanation: His repeated appearance for forty days emphasizes the ongoing threat.
challenge.q: What does the mention of forty days suggest?

answers: It explains that David belonged to a family whose three older sons were at the front
It explains why Jesse became king
It identifies Goliath as Jesse’s son
challenge.explanation: The family information explains David’s connection to the army and his position as the youngest at home.
challenge.q: Why is Jesse’s family described before the battle narrative continues?

paragraphs.title: David Is Sent to the Camp

easy.explanation: Jesse sent parched corn, loaves, and cheeses.
easy.q: What did Jesse send David to take to his brothers?

answers: Look how they fared and take their pledge
easy.explanation: Jesse told David to look how his brothers fared and take their pledge.
easy.q: What did Jesse tell David to do concerning his brothers?

answers: The men of Israel fleeing and greatly afraid
easy.explanation: The men of Israel fled from Goliath and were sore afraid.
easy.q: What did David see when he heard Goliath?

answers: His father sent him to check on his brothers
medium.explanation: David went because Jesse sent him to inquire about his brothers.
medium.q: Why did David go to the army’s camp?

answers: He left the sheep with a keeper
He brought the sheep into the camp
medium.explanation: David rose early and left the sheep with a keeper.
medium.q: What did David do before going to his brothers?

answers: Take responsibility for their welfare or bring back assurance about them
medium.explanation: Jesse wanted David to check on his brothers and bring back word of their condition.
medium.q: What does “take their pledge” mean in this context?

answers: He arrived just as the military confrontation was being renewed
He arrived before the armies gathered
challenge.explanation: David came as the host was going forth to fight and the armies were arranged.
challenge.q: What can be understood from David arriving as the battle was being set in array?

answers: He obeys the command and shows concern for his brothers
He refuses to leave the sheep
challenge.explanation: David did as Jesse commanded and went to inquire about his brothers.
challenge.q: How is David characterized in carrying out his errand?

answers: David’s errand brings him from tending sheep into the army’s camp
Saul sends David away from the palace
challenge.explanation: David’s assignment moves him from his shepherding duties into the conflict.
challenge.q: What connects the family story with the battle story?

paragraphs.title: The King’s Reward and David’s Willingness

answers: Great riches, the king’s daughter, and freedom for his father’s house
easy.explanation: The king promised great riches, his daughter, and freedom for the man’s father’s house.
easy.q: What was promised to the man who killed Goliath?

easy.explanation: Eliab’s anger was kindled against David.
easy.q: Who became angry with David?

easy.explanation: The people rehearsed David’s words before Saul, who sent for him.
easy.q: Before whom were David’s words eventually rehearsed?

answers: He wanted to understand what would be done for removing Israel’s reproach
He intended to surrender his brothers
medium.explanation: David asked about the reward for the man who would take away the reproach from Israel.
medium.q: Why did David ask again about the reward for defeating Goliath?

answers: To obey a command from Saul
medium.explanation: Eliab accused David of coming down so that he might see the battle.
medium.q: What did Eliab say was David’s reason for coming down?

answers: He left the camp at once
He answered briefly and continued asking about the matter
medium.explanation: David asked, “What have I now done? Is there not a cause?” and turned to speak with another.
medium.q: How did David respond to Eliab’s anger?

answers: Concern for Israel’s reproach and the armies of the living God
challenge.explanation: David was troubled that Goliath defied Israel and the armies of the living God.
challenge.q: What appears to motivate David when he speaks about Goliath?

answers: He focuses on the issue and does not let Eliab’s anger stop him
challenge.explanation: David does not allow the rebuke to end his inquiry about Goliath’s challenge.
challenge.q: What does David’s response to Eliab reveal about his conduct?

answers: He continued speaking about his willingness to face Goliath
Eliab ordered Saul to hear him
challenge.explanation: The people heard David’s words and rehearsed them before Saul.
challenge.q: Why did David’s words reach Saul?

easy.explanation: David told Saul that he would go and fight the Philistine.
easy.q: What did David offer to do?

easy.explanation: David said that he had delivered a lamb from a lion and a bear.
easy.q: From which animals did David deliver his father’s sheep?

answers: He wore it throughout the battle
He gave it to his brothers
easy.explanation: David removed the armor because he had not proved it.
easy.q: What did David do with Saul’s armor?

answers: David was a youth, while Goliath had been a man of war from his youth
David did not know his brothers
David had never visited the army
medium.explanation: Saul contrasted David’s youth with Goliath’s long experience as a warrior.
medium.q: Why did Saul think David could not fight Goliath?

answers: He showed that he had already faced danger bravely to protect the sheep
He asked Saul to bring him a lion
He argued that he needed no weapon at all
medium.explanation: David presented his experience rescuing sheep as evidence of his courage and ability.
medium.q: How did David use the story of the lion and bear?

answers: Armor, a helmet, and a sword
A staff, five stones, and a sling
A spear, shield, and coat of mail
medium.explanation: David took his staff, five smooth stones, shepherd’s bag, and sling.
medium.q: What did David choose to take into battle?

answers: Protecting the sheep had given him experience facing predators
Tending sheep kept him away from all danger
challenge.explanation: David’s defense of the flock prepared him to face another threatening enemy.
challenge.q: What connection does David make between tending sheep and fighting Goliath?

answers: He had not proved it and was not accustomed to it
Saul took it back before the battle
challenge.explanation: David said, “I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them.”
challenge.q: Why did David remove Saul’s armor?

answers: He relied on familiar tools and his own experience
He did not intend to fight
challenge.explanation: David chose the staff, stones, and sling that he knew how to use.
challenge.q: What does David’s choice of shepherd’s equipment emphasize?

paragraphs.title: David and Goliath Face Each Other

easy.explanation: Goliath disdained David because he was only a youth.
easy.q: How did Goliath react when he saw David?

answers: In the name of the LORD of hosts
easy.explanation: David declared that he came in the name of the LORD of hosts.
easy.q: In whose name did David say he came?

answers: That there is a God in Israel
That Goliath was stronger than Israel
easy.explanation: David said that all the earth would know there is a God in Israel.
easy.q: What would the victory show?

answers: A sword, a spear, and a shield
medium.explanation: David said, “Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield.”
medium.q: What weapons did Goliath say David was coming against?

answers: Smite him and take his head from him
medium.explanation: David declared that the LORD would deliver Goliath into his hand and that he would take his head.
medium.q: What did David say he would do to Goliath?

answers: Victory depends only on the amount of weapons
The battle belongs to the LORD, who is able to save
medium.explanation: David taught that deliverance does not depend merely on sword and spear.
medium.q: What does “the battle is the LORD’S” mean?

answers: Goliath trusts in weapons, while David comes in the name of the LORD
Goliath is young and David is old
challenge.explanation: David contrasts Goliath’s weapons with his reliance on the LORD.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast in David’s words to Goliath?

answers: To gain the king’s reward alone
To show Israel and the earth that the LORD saves
To make David captain of the army
challenge.explanation: David said the result would make all the earth know that there is a God in Israel.
challenge.q: What was the ultimate purpose of David’s expected victory?

answers: He says the challenge is a reproach against God’s armies and that the LORD will decide the battle
He asks Goliath to join Israel
challenge.explanation: David interprets Goliath’s challenge as defiance of the living God and trusts the LORD for victory.
challenge.q: How does David turn Goliath’s threat into a statement of faith?

paragraphs.title: David’s Victory and the Philistine Flight

easy.explanation: David slung a stone that struck Goliath in the forehead.
easy.q: What struck Goliath in the forehead?

answers: He fell upon his face to the earth
easy.explanation: The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell upon his face.
easy.q: What happened to Goliath after the stone struck him?

easy.explanation: When they saw their champion was dead, they fled.
easy.q: What did the Philistines do when they saw their champion was dead?

medium.explanation: David took Goliath’s sword and used it to slay him and cut off his head.
medium.q: What weapon did David use to kill Goliath after bringing him down?

answers: They pursued them and spoiled their tents
They gave the Philistines their weapons
medium.explanation: Israel pursued the Philistines and later spoiled their tents.
medium.q: What did the men of Israel and Judah do after the Philistines fled?

answers: He left it in the field
medium.explanation: David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem.
medium.q: What did David do with Goliath’s head?

answers: He first prevailed through the sling and stone before taking Goliath’s sword
He did not fight at all
challenge.explanation: The text emphasizes that the initial victory came through the sling and stone.
challenge.q: What does the statement that David had no sword in his hand emphasize?

answers: The Philistines fled and Israel pursued them
Israel retreated while the Philistines plundered the camp
challenge.explanation: The death of the Philistine champion caused the Philistines to flee and Israel to pursue.
challenge.q: How did Goliath’s fall affect the two armies?

answers: The sword completed the victory after Goliath had been struck down
David returned the sword to Goliath
The sword was used only for decoration
challenge.explanation: David first felled Goliath with the stone and then used the giant’s sword to finish the victory.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between David taking Goliath’s sword and cutting off his head?

easy.explanation: Saul asked Abner whose son the youth was.
easy.q: Whom did Saul ask about David’s identity?

answers: No, he said he could not tell
He thought David was Saul’s son
easy.explanation: Abner answered, “As thy soul liveth, O king, I cannot tell.”
easy.q: Did Abner know whose son David was?

easy.explanation: David identified himself as the son of Jesse the Bethlehemite.
easy.q: Whose son did David say he was?

answers: Before David came to the camp
When Saul saw David go forth against the Philistine
medium.explanation: Saul asked Abner when he saw David go forth against Goliath.
medium.q: When did Saul ask about David’s identity?

medium.explanation: Abner took David and brought him before Saul.
medium.q: Who brought David before Saul after the battle?

medium.explanation: David came before Saul with the Philistine’s head in his hand.
medium.q: What was David carrying when he was brought before Saul?

answers: David was not yet well known to them despite his great deed
challenge.explanation: Their questions show that David’s family identity was not known to them at that moment.
challenge.q: What may be inferred from Saul and Abner not knowing David’s family connection?

answers: David has defeated the Philistine champion, yet Saul still asks who he is
David fled from battle, yet everyone knew him
David was king, yet he had no army
challenge.explanation: Although David had accomplished a remarkable victory, Saul still sought to learn his family background.
challenge.q: What contrast is created between David’s deed and Saul’s question?

answers: As the son of Jesse the Bethlehemite
As the captain of Israel’s army
challenge.explanation: David answers simply that he is the son of Jesse the Bethlehemite.
challenge.q: How does David present himself in his answer to Saul?
